name: docker
summary: Build, run and manage containers and images.

modes.name: run
modes.summary: Create and start a container from an image.

modes.name: create
modes.summary: Create a container without starting it.

modes.name: exec
modes.summary: Run a command inside a container that is already running.

modes.name: build
modes.summary: Build an image from a Dockerfile.

modes.name: pull
modes.summary: Download an image from a registry.

modes.name: push
modes.summary: Upload an image to a registry.

modes.name: logs
modes.summary: Show the output of a container.

modes.name: inspect
modes.summary: Print everything the daemon knows about an object, as JSON.

modes.name: cp
modes.summary: Copy files between a container and the host.

modes.name: start
modes.summary: Start a stopped container.

modes.name: stop
modes.summary: Stop a running container.

modes.name: restart
modes.summary: Restart a container.

modes.name: kill
modes.summary: Send a signal to a container.

modes.name: rm
modes.summary: Remove a container.

modes.name: rmi
modes.summary: Remove an image.

modes.name: commit
modes.summary: Make an image from a container’s current state.

modes.name: save
modes.summary: Write an image to a tar archive.

modes.name: tag
modes.summary: Give an image another name.

modes.name: search
modes.summary: Search Docker Hub for images.

modes.name: port
modes.summary: Show the port mappings of a container.

modes.name: top
modes.summary: Show the processes running inside a container.

modes.name: diff
modes.summary: Show what has changed in a container’s filesystem.

modes.name: export
modes.summary: Write a container’s filesystem to a tar archive.

modes.name: import
modes.summary: Make an image from a tar archive.

modes.name: attach
modes.summary: Attach your terminal to a running container.

modes.name: pause
modes.summary: Suspend every process in a container.

modes.name: unpause
modes.summary: Resume a paused container.

modes.name: rename
modes.summary: Rename a container.

modes.name: update
modes.summary: Change the resource limits of a running container.

modes.name: wait
modes.summary: Block until a container stops, then print its exit code.

modes.name: history
modes.summary: Show the layers an image is built from.

modes.name: ps
modes.summary: List containers.

modes.name: images
modes.summary: List images.

recipes.name: Shell into a throwaway container
recipes.summary: Interactive terminal, removed the moment you exit. The one you reach for most.
recipes.when: You want a clean Linux box for two minutes.
recipes.cost: Pulls the image the first time. Nothing is left behind.

recipes.name: Run a service in the background
recipes.summary: Detached, named, with a port published to the host and a restart policy.
recipes.when: Standing something up you want to keep running.
recipes.cost: Runs until stopped. --restart brings it back after a reboot.

recipes.name: Run with your code mounted in
recipes.summary: Bind-mounts a directory from the host so edits are seen inside.
recipes.when: Developing against a container rather than installing a toolchain.
recipes.cost: The container writes to your real files. That is the point, and the risk.

recipes.name: Run with environment variables
recipes.summary: Passes configuration in, which is how most images expect to be set up.
recipes.when: Database passwords, API keys, anything the image reads from the environment.
recipes.cost: Values given with -e are visible in docker inspect. Prefer --env-file.

recipes.name: Run with resource limits
recipes.summary: Caps memory and CPU so one container cannot take the machine.
recipes.when: Anything untrusted, or anything you have seen misbehave.
recipes.cost: The container is killed if it exceeds the memory limit.

recipes.name: Run with the brakes on
recipes.summary: Read-only filesystem, no new privileges, every capability dropped.
recipes.when: Running something you do not fully trust.
recipes.cost: Many images need a writable /tmp — add --tmpfs /tmp if it fails.

recipes.name: Get a shell in a running container
recipes.summary: Opens an interactive shell in a container that is already up.
recipes.when: Debugging something that is running now.
recipes.cost: Changes you make vanish when the container is replaced.

recipes.name: Shell in as root
recipes.summary: Same, but as root — for when the image runs as an unprivileged user.
recipes.when: You need to install a tool inside a container to diagnose it.
recipes.cost: Root inside the container. Treat it accordingly.

recipes.name: Follow the logs
recipes.summary: Streams output as it happens, with timestamps, starting from the last 100 lines.
recipes.when: Watching a service start, or catching an error as it happens.
recipes.cost: Runs until you stop it.

recipes.name: Everything the daemon knows
recipes.summary: Full JSON for a container, image, network or volume.
recipes.when: Finding the real mounts, ports, environment or IP address.
recipes.cost: Long output. Add --format to pull out one field.

recipes.name: Just the IP address
recipes.summary: A Go template that extracts one field instead of printing everything.
recipes.when: You want one value, usually for a script.
recipes.cost: None.

recipes.name: Every container, running or not
recipes.summary: Includes stopped containers, which is usually what you actually wanted.
recipes.when: Something exited and you want to know why.
recipes.cost: None.

recipes.name: A readable container table
recipes.summary: Only the columns worth seeing, instead of the full-width default.
recipes.when: The default output wraps and you cannot read it.
recipes.cost: None.

recipes.name: Build an image
recipes.summary: Builds the Dockerfile in the current directory and names the result.
recipes.when: The ordinary build.
recipes.cost: Uses the cache. Minutes the first time.

recipes.name: Build without the cache
recipes.summary: Ignores cached layers and re-pulls the base image.
recipes.when: The build succeeded but produced something stale.
recipes.cost: Slow, by design.

recipes.name: Build with build arguments
recipes.summary: Passes values into the Dockerfile and targets one stage of a multi-stage build.
recipes.when: One Dockerfile that builds several ways.
recipes.cost: Build args are visible in the image history. Never pass secrets this way.

recipes.name: Copy a file out of a container
recipes.summary: Works on stopped containers too, which makes it good for post-mortems.
recipes.when: Retrieving a log or an artefact.
recipes.cost: None.

recipes.name: Save an image to a file
recipes.summary: Writes a tar you can carry to a machine with no registry access.
recipes.when: Air-gapped environments, or sending an image to someone.
recipes.cost: As large as the image.

recipes.name: Download an image
recipes.summary: Fetches an image from a registry without running anything.
recipes.when: Pre-pulling before you need it, or refreshing a tag.
recipes.cost: Downloads. Size depends on the image.

recipes.name: Remove a container, running or not
recipes.summary: Forces removal and takes its anonymous volumes with it.
recipes.when: Clearing out something stuck.
recipes.cost: Destructive. --volumes deletes anonymous volume data permanently.

recipes.name: Stop, with a grace period
recipes.summary: Sends SIGTERM, waits, then SIGKILL — thirty seconds instead of the default ten.
recipes.when: A service that needs time to finish what it is doing.
recipes.cost: Up to thirty seconds.
